2027-04-03.title: First Saturday of Resurrection
2027-04-03.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
2027-04-03.alt: Season of the Resurrection (Qyamta). The last day of the first week of the Resurrection, the week of the newly baptised. Tomorrow is New Sunday (Puthu Njayar), the Second Sunday of Resurrection.
2027-04-03.verse: For you have died, and your life is hidden with Christ in God.
theo: On the last day of Easter week the Church goes back once more to the tomb, this time with Mark. “When the sabbath was over, Mary Magdalene, and Mary the mother of James, and Salome bought spices, so that they might go and anoint him.” They are going to do the last thing love can do for the dead. On the way they have one worry: “Who will roll away the stone for us from the entrance to the tomb?” It is a real problem; Mark tells us the stone “was very large”. But “When they looked up, they saw that the stone, which was very large, had already been rolled back.” How much of our life is spent walking towards a stone that God has already moved. We lie awake over a conversation we fear, a sin we cannot confess, a reconciliation we think impossible, and when we finally arrive, the stone is gone. Inside the tomb a young man in a white robe gives the Easter announcement: “Do not be alarmed; you are looking for Jesus of Nazareth, who was crucified. He has been raised; he is not here. Look, there is the place they laid him.” The angel points to an empty place. The Church has never preached a Resurrection of the spirit only, or a Christ who lives on merely in the memory of his friends. The body that was laid there is gone because it has been raised, the same body that bore the nails, now glorified. The Gospels do not tell us that the Risen Lord appeared first to his Mother, but an old and loving tradition of the Church, among Eastern and Western writers alike, has believed that he did, and that Mary, who kept faith through the long Saturday, was the first to be filled with the joy of her Son's Resurrection.

Then the commission: “But go, tell his disciples and Peter that he is going ahead of you to Galilee; there you will see him, just as he told you.” Two words have consoled sinners for twenty centuries: and Peter. Peter, who had sworn he did not know the man; Peter, who had wept in the courtyard. He is named on purpose, so that he will not think he has been struck off the list. The Risen Lord does not send a message to the faithful disciples and leave out the one who failed. And he sends them back to Galilee, where it all began, by the lake where he first called them. He is “going ahead of you”: wherever we go, he is there first. Mark's Gospel then ends in a strange way: “So they went out and fled from the tomb, for terror and amazement had seized them; and they said nothing to anyone, for they were afraid.” The oldest manuscripts of Mark stop here; the Church receives the longer ending (Mark 16:9–20) as inspired Scripture, and it tells of the appearances that followed. But the silence of verse 8 is itself a message. The news was too great for them at first; fear held them. Yet we know the end of the story: the women did speak, the disciples did see him in Galilee, and the news has reached Kerala and every continent. Fear was not the last word. Every Christian who hears the Easter Gospel is asked to finish the sentence the women left unfinished, by telling someone.

Paul tells the newly baptised what to do with the Easter news in daily life. “So if you have been raised with Christ, seek the things that are above, where Christ is, seated at the right hand of God. Set your minds on things that are above, not on things that are on earth.” This is not an escape from the world; Paul goes on in the same chapter to speak of family life, work and forgiveness. It is a question of where the heart is fixed. Every Holy Qurbana, before the great prayer of the anaphora, the priest calls us to lift up our minds on high, and we answer that they are turned towards the God of Abraham, Isaac and Israel. Then the deepest line: “for you have died, and your life is hidden with Christ in God. When Christ who is your life is revealed, then you also will be revealed with him in glory.” Tomorrow, on New Sunday, the newly baptised of the ancient Church laid aside the white garments they had worn all week. The white robe was put away, but the new life was not; it went on, hidden, like a seed under the soil, like a treasure in a locked box, like the life of the Lord himself for thirty years at Nazareth. Most of the holiness in the world is hidden: a mother's prayers for a son abroad, a nurse's patience on a night shift, an old man's rosary in an empty church. None of it is lost. It is hidden with Christ in God, and on the last day it will be revealed with him in glory.
conn: An angel rolls back the stone and sits on it (Matthew 28:2); the stone was “very large” (Mark 16:4); “Weeping may linger for the night, but joy comes with the morning” (Psalm 30:5).
The first day of the week.

God began creation on the first day (Genesis 1:3–5); the women come “very early on the first day of the week” (Mark 16:2); the first Christians gathered on the first day of the week to break bread (Acts 20:7).
Jesus prayed that Peter's faith would not fail (Luke 22:31–32); Peter wept after his denial (Luke 22:61–62); the Risen Lord asks him three times, “do you love me?” (John 21:15–17).

“Galilee of the Gentiles… the people who sat in darkness have seen a great light” (Matthew 4:15–16); the Risen Lord meets the Eleven on a mountain in Galilee and sends them to all nations (Matthew 28:16–20).
“The LORD says to my lord, ‘Sit at my right hand’” (Psalm 110:1); Stephen sees Jesus standing at the right hand of God (Acts 7:56).
“he will hide me in his shelter in the day of trouble” (Psalm 27:5); “your Father who sees in secret will reward you” (Matthew 6:6).
altar: The women came with spices for a dead body and found the Living One. At the Holy Qurbana we do not come to honour a memory: the Lord who rose bodily from the tomb gives us his true Body and Blood, alive and glorified.

Before the anaphora the priest invites us to lift up our minds on high. To seek the things that are above, Paul's Easter command, is what we do at every Qurbana, where heaven and earth meet on the altar.
outline: A woman lying awake over a conversation she dreads.
Point 1 · Who will roll away the stone?
The women's worry and the stone already moved.
Point 2 · He has been raised; he is not here
The empty place and the bodily Resurrection.
Point 3 · Tell his disciples and Peter
The one who failed is named first.
Point 4 · Hidden with Christ in God
Seeking the things above; the hidden holiness of every day.
White baptismal robes folded and put away, and a life that goes on.
“Your life is hidden with Christ in God.”
live: Take one step this week towards a reconciliation or a confession you have been dreading; trust that God goes before you.
If you feel you have failed God, read Mark 16:7 slowly and put your own name after ‘and’.
Before you open your phone in the morning, lift your mind to God with one short prayer.
Thank one person this week whose quiet faithfulness nobody notices.
fathers: Why did the angel name Peter alone? Because if he had not been named, Peter, who had denied his Master, might have thought himself unworthy to come among the disciples. So he is called by name, so that he may not despair because of his denial. Let us consider how great is the mercy of God, who does not let the fallen be lost but calls him back by name.

When you hear, Lift up your hearts, and you answer that you have them lifted up to the Lord, let your answer be true. Our Head has gone up into heaven; let the members follow in desire. While the body is still on earth, the heart can already be where Christ is, and our life is hidden there with him until he appears.
magis: The empty tomb and the linen cloths lying there signify that the body of Christ escaped the bonds of death by God's power.
Mary Magdalene and the holy women were the first to encounter the Risen One and the first messengers of the Resurrection, even to the apostles.
Peter, chosen to confirm the faith of his brothers, saw the Risen One before them; on his witness the community exclaims, ‘The Lord has risen indeed’.
The Resurrection of Christ is the principle and source of our future resurrection.
United with Christ by Baptism, believers already share in his risen life; but this life remains hidden with Christ in God.
saints: Saturday 3 April closes the first week of Resurrection, the week of the newly baptised. Tomorrow, Sunday 4 April: New Sunday (Puthu Njayar), the confession of St Thomas, and in many places the great pilgrimage to the Kurisumudi at Malayattoor.
2027-04-03.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, you rolled away the stone that we feared, and you left the tomb empty because you are risen in the body. You sent word to your disciples and to Peter, so that no one who has failed would think himself forgotten. Raise our minds to the things that are above, where you are seated at the right hand of the Father. Keep our life hidden with you in God, and when you appear, let us appear with you in glory. Through the prayers of your holy Mother, who kept faith through the long Saturday, fill us with Easter joy. Glory to you, with the Father and the Holy Spirit, for ever. Amen. Alleluia!

quick: The women ask, “Who will roll away the stone?” and find it already rolled back.
The angel: he has been raised; he is not here; go, tell his disciples and Peter.
Paul: seek the things that are above; your life is hidden with Christ in God.
2027-04-03.action: Take one step today towards the ‘stone’ you have been dreading.
2027-04-03.question: What stone am I worrying about that God may already have moved?
catechism: The women and Peter, first witnesses.
Risen with Christ, hidden with him.
kidsaint: Peter loved Jesus, but on the night before Jesus died he was afraid and said three times, ‘I do not know him!’ Afterwards he cried bitterly. On Easter morning the angel said: go and tell the disciples and Peter. Jesus wanted Peter to know he was still his friend. Later Jesus made him the shepherd of the whole Church. Lesson: when you make a mistake, Jesus calls you back by name!
2027-04-03.special: First Saturday of Resurrection. The last day of Easter week, the week of the newly baptised.
term: The Syriac name for Sunday, ‘the first day of the week’, the phrase the Gospels use for the morning of the Resurrection (Mark 16:2). For the East Syriac Church every Sunday is a little Easter, the day of the Risen Lord.

family.explain: Early on Sunday morning three women walked to Jesus' tomb. They were worried: “Who will roll away the big stone for us?” But when they got there, the stone was already rolled away! An angel in white said: “Jesus is not here. He is risen!” Sometimes we worry about things, but God is already there to help us. We can tell Jesus our worries, and trust him.
family.intention: We pray that our family may trust Jesus with all our worries, because he is risen and goes ahead of us.
family.ask: Ask: “What is one ‘big stone’ I am worried about? Let's give it to Jesus now.”

illus: For three years a man in Thodupuzha had not spoken to his younger brother after a quarrel over a strip of rubber land. Every Easter his wife asked him to make peace, and every Easter he said, ‘He will throw me out.’ That year, on the Saturday after Easter, he finally walked the two kilometres to his brother's house, rehearsing what he would say. He stopped at the gate, almost turned back, and then saw that the gate was open and his brother was standing in the yard. ‘I was coming to you tomorrow, after the Qurbana,’ the brother said. ‘I have been wanting to for a year.’ They sat on the verandah until dark. On the way home the man laughed out loud. ‘The whole road I was asking who would roll away the stone,’ he told his wife, ‘and it was already open.’

pm.open: Risen Lord, you go ahead of us into every Galilee. Lift up our minds to you as we pray together. Amen. Alleluia!
share: Who will roll away the stone for us? (Mark 16:3). What am I afraid to face?
He has been raised; he is not here (Mark 16:6). How does the empty tomb change the way I look at death?
Go, tell his disciples and Peter (Mark 16:7). Do I believe that Christ calls me back after I have failed?
Your life is hidden with Christ in God (Colossians 3:3). Where do I see hidden holiness around me?
pm.resp: Lord, we seek you above all things.
interc: For those who are afraid of a stone in their lives, a confession, a reconciliation, an illness, that they may find it rolled away.
For all who have denied or abandoned the Lord, that they may hear him call them by name as he called Peter.
For the newly baptised, as Easter week ends, that their new life may continue hidden with Christ.
For mothers and grandmothers whose hidden prayers hold their families together.
For pilgrims going up to Malayattoor and to all the shrines of Mar Thoma this New Sunday.
pm.close: Father, you raised your Son from the dead and seated him at your right hand. Keep our hearts fixed on him, forgive us when we fail, and on the last day reveal us with him in glory. Through Christ our Lord. Amen. Alleluia!

homily: Dear friends, three women walk to the tomb at sunrise with spices and one worry: “Who will roll away the stone for us?” It was a real worry; the stone was very large. But when they looked up, it had already been rolled back.

How often we are like them. We worry for weeks about a conversation, a confession, a reconciliation, and when we finally go, God has already gone ahead and moved the stone. Easter teaches us to walk towards the stone.

The angel says: “He has been raised; he is not here. Look, there is the place they laid him.” The tomb is empty because the Lord is risen in his body. He is not a memory. He is alive, and we meet him at this altar.

Then: “go, tell his disciples and Peter.” Why Peter? Because Peter had denied him. The Lord did not want Peter to think he was finished. If you have failed, put your own name there: tell the disciples, and tell me.

Paul adds: “seek the things that are above… for you have died, and your life is hidden with Christ in God.” The newly baptised will take off their white garments, but their new life goes on, hidden. So does ours: in quiet prayers, faithful work, patient love. None of it is lost; it will be revealed with him in glory.
Tomorrow is New Sunday, the Sunday of Mar Thoma. Today let us take one step towards our stone, and lift up our minds to the Lord. Christ is risen! Alleluia! Amen.
kids: Children, the women were worried: ‘Who will move the big stone?’ But God had already moved it, and Jesus was risen!
When you are worried, tell Jesus. He is already there to help you.

The stone already rolled away, the empty place, the message to Peter, and the hidden life of the baptised.

q: Who is a God like you, pardoning iniquity and passing over the transgression of the remnant of your possession? He does not retain his anger forever, because he delights in showing clemency.
But go, tell his disciples and Peter that he is going ahead of you to Galilee; there you will see him, just as he told you.

points.h: Seek the things that are above
q: My help comes from the LORD, who made heaven and earth.
So if you have been raised with Christ, seek the things that are above, where Christ is, seated at the right hand of God.
points.apply: Begin each morning this week by lifting your mind to God before anything else.

q: For he will hide me in his shelter in the day of trouble; he will conceal me under the cover of his tent; he will set me high on a rock.
for you have died, and your life is hidden with Christ in God. When Christ who is your life is revealed, then you also will be revealed with him in glory.
points.apply: Thank one person whose hidden faithfulness holds your family or parish together.

concl: The stone is rolled away, the tomb is empty, and the Lord calls back even those who failed him.
Our new life is hidden with him now, and will be revealed with him in glory.
2027-04-03.resolve: This week, walk towards one stone you fear, pray the ‘Queen of Heaven’ each day, and lift your mind to God before you open your phone each morning.
